snippet.title: Mushrooms for the Mind & Immune System | Paul Stamets
snippet.description:
Paul Stamets is widely regarded as the father of modern applied mycology for his work on fungi and their applications in human health. We discuss how mushrooms and other fungi affect, and can improve, our immune system; how certain non-psychedelic mushrooms can enhance cognition and brain plasticity; and the use of psilocybin for depression, anxiety, and other mental health conditions, as well as important safety considerations. This episode is for anyone seeking to learn more about the biology of fungi and their medicinal and other uses.

snippet.title: Essentials: How Emotions & Social Factors Impact Learning | Dr. Mary Helen Immordino-Yang
snippet.description:
In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, my guest is Dr. Mary Helen Immordino-Yang, EdD, a professor of education and psychology at the University of Southern California (USC) and director of the USC Center for Affective Neuroscience, Development, Learning and Education (CANDLE). We discuss how emotions, stories and culture shape the way we perceive the world, learn and build a sense of self. We also explain how our narratives can foster empathy or dehumanization, and how education can be redesigned to engage curiosity, meaning-making and the development of the whole person.

Dr. Søberg explains how brief, deliberate cold exposure improves insulin sensitivity, promotes metabolic health and physiological resilience. We also discuss the cold shock response and shivering, along with practical guidance on temperature, duration, and sequencing cold and heat exposure for optimal benefits.

 In this ⁠Huberman Lab Essentials⁠ episode, I explain the biology, symptoms and types of bipolar disorder (sometimes called bipolar depression), a condition characterized by extreme, maladaptive shifts in energy, mood and perception. I describe the diagnostic criteria that distinguish bipolar I from bipolar II, including mania and hypomania and the different patterns of mood cycling. I discuss the remarkable history and discovery of lithium and how it works, in part by reducing inflammation, providing neuroprotection and supporting the interoceptive neural circuits affected in bipolar disorder. I also cover talk therapies, electroconvulsive therapy and nutraceuticals such as omega-3 fatty acids and inositol, and I explore the intriguing relationship between mood disorders and creativity. This episode should interest anyone who has or knows someone with bipolar disorder, as well as those interested in how the brain balances mood, energy and focus.

snippet.description:
See Andrew Huberman live in New York, Los Angeles & San Francisco:
https://go.hubermanlab.com/protocols-event

 In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, I explain the neuroscience of grief, including how the brain maps relationships across three dimensions — space, time, and closeness — and why losing someone requires a remapping of those neural circuits. I describe how grief differs from depression, the role of oxytocin in driving yearning after a loss, and why people move through grief at different rates. I also discuss science-based tools for grieving adaptively, including how to access feelings of attachment while decoupling them from episodic memory. Finally, I explain how foundational biology — particularly sleep and cortisol rhythms — shapes our capacity to navigate the grieving process.
